answer: Not as far as your records show. The CT scan of your chest on July 8, 2025 found no blood clot in your lungs, and the report says your lungs were clear. A clot in the lungs (pulmonary embolism) was on your problem list from that visit, but it was later marked as ruled out, so it is not recorded as a real diagnosis. The visit was for chest pain, which was diagnosed as chest wall pain and was marked resolved by July 22, 2025. A blood test that day (D-dimer) came back high. A high D-dimer is not specific to clots and can be raised by many other things; the scan is what settled the question. Nothing later in your records mentions a clot in the lungs. If you get new chest pain, shortness of breath or leg swelling, tell your doctor promptly.
